query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing Fe as a dopant into a Mn-rich Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloy will enhance its magnetocaloric effect by sharpening the magnetostructural transition.
generation.intervention: Doping the alloy with controlled amounts of Fe to partially substitute Ni sites
generation.conditions: Experiments performed near room temperature under applied magnetic fields
generation.structural_mediator: Modification of lattice parameters and enhancement of magnetostructural coupling
generation.mechanism: Fe doping is expected to alter the exchange interactions in the alloy, promoting a sharper, more cooperative phase transition accompanied by reduced thermal hysteresis. This should result in an increased magnetic entropy change.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Fe-doped Heusler alloy will show a higher magnetic entropy change and reduced thermal hysteresis compared to the undoped Mn-rich Ni-Mn-In alloy under similar magnetic field conditions.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected within a limited doping range and for specific temperature windows close to room temperature; effects outside these parameters remain uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: Precise optimal Fe concentration and quantitative improvements in magnetocaloric properties are uncertain without experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of Mn-rich Ni-Mn-In Heusler alloys with varying Fe doping levels (e.g., 0%, 2%, 5%, 10%). Characterize their magnetocaloric properties by measuring the magnetic entropy change (ΔS_m) and thermal hysteresis across the transition temperature under controlled magnetic field sweeps near room temperature.
measurements: Magnetization curves as a function of temperature and field
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Fe-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant enhancement in ΔS_m or reduction in thermal hysteresis compared to the undoped alloy under identical conditions, the hypothesis will be falsified.
